result.description:
The Client  

Taigum Child Edu-care Centre in Taigum, QLD is a reputable childcare centre who provides impactful guidance for young children through their early childhood development stages.  

 

 

The Role 

The role for hire is an Early Childhood Teacher based in Taigum, QLD, it is a full-time role with an annual salary set between $83,000 to $86,000 depending on experience plus superannuation. 

 

 

The Responsibilities  

Develop and implement child-care programs that support and promote the physical, cognitive, emotional and social development of children 

Lead activities by telling or reading stories, teaching songs, taking children to local points of interest and providing opportunities to express creativity through the media of art, dramatic play, music and physical activity 

Plan and maintain an environment that protects the health, security and well-being of children 

Assess the abilities, interests and needs of children and discuss progress or problems with parents and other staff members 

Observe children for signs of potential learning or behavioural problems and prepare reports for parents, guardians or supervisor 

Guide and assist children in the development of proper eating, dressing and toilet habits 

Establish and maintain collaborative relationships with co-workers and community service providers working with children 

May plan and organize activities for school-age children in child-care programs before and after regular school hours 

May supervise and co-ordinate activities of other early childhood educators and early childhood educator assistants. 

Early childhood educator assistants perform some or all of the following duties: 

Support early childhood educators in carrying out programs that promote the physical, cognitive, emotional and social development of children 

Engage children in activities by telling stories, teaching songs and preparing crafts 

Prepare snacks and arrange rooms or furniture for lunch and rest periods 

Assist with proper eating, dressing and toilet habits 

Submit written observations on children to early childhood educators or supervisors 

Maintain daycare equipment and assist in housekeeping and cooking duties 

 

 

The Requirements 

Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care (or equivalent) 

First Aid Qualifications and Training as prescribed by the Education and Care Services National Law Act 2010 (CPR, Asthma & Anaphylaxis, General First Aid) 

At least 12 months of professional experience in early childhood teaching in Australia 

At least 12 months’ experience teaching in early childhood education settings, delivering programs aligned with EYLF and NQS. 

At least 12 months’ experience in curriculum development, child assessment, and educational programming. 

At least 12 months’ experience mentoring and supervising educators in early childhood pedagogy and best practices. 

At least 12 months’ experience supporting children with diverse learning needs and implementing inclusive teaching strategies. 

At least 12 months’ experience liaising with parents, carers, and external agencies to support children’s learning outcomes. 

Thorough knowledge of the National Quality Framework 

A current knowledge of relevant curriculum frameworks and the ability to implement a program that caters to diversity amongst the children, educators, families and community 

A working knowledge and thorough understanding of the national quality standards, the education and care services national law act 2010 and the education and care services national regulations 2011 

Well-developed communication and inter-personal skills with children, adults, fellow educators and the community 

Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment, being sensitive to the strength and weaknesses of fellow team members

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     About the role

Join Wesley Mission Queensland as a Disability Support Worker in our Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA) team.

This is hands-on, meaningful work where you support vulnerable people with disability to build independence in their everyday lives.

In this role, you will:

Led by Registered Nurses

Trained to practice High Intensity Supports (i.e. Dysphasia management, Epilepsy, Tracheostomy).

Provide personal care and daily living support (meals, hygiene, household tasks)

Support individuals to build independence and life skills

Assist with community access and participation

Work collaboratively with a team to deliver active supports and, person-centred care

What your day can look like

No two days are the same. You might:

Help someone cook their first independent meal

Support a resident to confidently leave home and access the community

Deliver responsive support to individuals with complex needs, ensuring they feel safe and supported.

Build trust through everyday routines, conversations, and shared activities

This is practical, real work where you can see the impact you make.

What's in it for you

Free secure on-site parking

Career progression across various "internal" disability support programs or the wider WMQ business

Ongoing training & development

Supportive team environment where colleagues' step in and help

Work for a values-driven not-for-profit organisation

Permanent DSW Pay Rates:

Mon-Fri (AM shifts): $36.22-hr

Mon-Fri (Afternoon shifts): $40.75-hr

Mon-Fri (Night shifts): $41.65-hr

Saturday: $54.33-hr

Sunday: $72.44-hr

Public Holidays: $90.55-hr

Sleepover allowance: $62.11

Let's be honest
This is a highly rewarding role within a complex support environment.

You'll work alongside people with diverse and sometimes complex support needs

Every day brings different situations and opportunities to make a difference

Building trust, skills, and independence takes time and consistency

The reward is seeing the progress people make and knowing you played a part in helping them achieve their goals

About you

We're looking for reliable, genuine people who want to build a career in disability support.

You will have:

A caring, respectful, and patient approach

Ability to stay calm under pressure

Strong communication and teamwork skills

A genuine interest in supporting people to live independently

Requirements

Certificate III in Individual Support (Disability) or equivalent

Current Australian Driver's Licence - with full comprehensive motor vehicle insurance

NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (or willingness to obtain)

Current First Aid & CPR

Strong written and verbal communication skills

About the service

Our Supported Disability Accommodation is more than a service - it's a home.

We focus on:

Supporting choice and independence

Building confidence through everyday routines

Creating a safe, consistent, and respectful environment

About Wesley Mission Queensland

Wesley Mission Queensland is a not-for-profit organisation supporting people across disability, aged care, mental health, and community services for over 100 years.

We focus on:

Practical, person-centred support

Building independence and wellbeing

Supporting our employees as well as the people we serve

Apply now

If you're looking for:

A Disability Support Worker role with real impact

A supportive, team-based environment

Click Apply Now to join Wesley Mission Queensland.    Click here to Apply now →

ABOUT US
As Australia's leading environmentally focused service business, delivering on modern thinking and action to prevent, stop and reverse environmental damage, our core focus is to create safe and sustainable environments within communities. Behind our success is a very talented and inclusive team of diverse individuals that you too could join, bringing your knowledge, experience, skills, and attributes that will only make the foundation of our company, our people, even stronger.

Through our values of People First, Collaboration, Creative Thinking and Customer Focus, we work to help our people achieve our goals and enjoy their work. We are an Equal Opportunity employer and are committed to creating an equitable , diverse and inclusive work environment for all. We recognise that diversity strengthens us and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply, including women and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

ABOUT THE ROLE
We are seeking an Operator / Leading Hand to join our projects team.

You will be responsible for supporting the delivery of site works on unique and exciting projects across Darwin and the broader NT.

As an Operator /  Leading Hand, you will be responsible for the following:
Supervision and operation of plant, labour, and subcontractors.
Supporting Supervisors in planning and co-ordination of site work.
Enforcing and demonstrating safe work practices in all site-related works.
Ensuring that personnel are adequately trained and supported.
Assist the Project Manager and Project Engineers with site operations.

ABOUT YOU
You will be an experienced Operator / Leading Hand who has a background in either supervision, or Plant Operations on civil or environmental remediation projects. 

You will have:
5+ years experience working on Civil or Remediation projects.
Earthworks experience.
Demonstrated ability to take a hands-on approach on site.
Asbestos Removal tickets, advantageous but not essential.
Plant Operation tickets.
Drivers licence.
Australian Citizenship. 

WHAT WE GIVE YOU IN RETURN
Rewarding and important work that makes a difference to the community and the environment.

We prioritise your Health and Wellbeing:
Four paid annual Wellbeing Days, we give you additional time off to do the things that you love with the people you love.
Employee assistance program, a free counselling and lifestyle service for you and your family.

We care about your future with us:
Propel your career: Unlock your potential with tailored and ongoing professional development and internal job opportunities to ensure you stay ahead in your field.

We offer competitive rewards and benefits:
Rewarding Referrals: Your recommendations matter to us. Our generous employee referral incentive program is instrumental in building a team of like-minded individuals that share our company values.
Celebrating our Champions: We acknowledge and celebrate our employees' achievements in supporting our company principles through the monthly and annual Enviro Achiever awards.?
Enhancing your Lifestyle: We offer paid primary and secondary carer leave, novated leases, flexible work arrangements and purchased leave.

We acknowledges the Traditional Owners of the land where we work and live. We pay our respects to Elders past, present and emerging. We are committed to strengthening relationships between Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and non-Indigenous peoples for the benefit of all Australians.
